source.title: Sharp-MAML: Sharpness-Aware Model-Agnostic Meta Learning
source.authors: Momin Abbas; Quan-Wu Xiao; Lisha Chen; Pin-Yu Chen; Tianyi Chen

record.tranche_reason: Applies sharpness-aware training in the new setting of MAML and reports held-out task performance; it does not test the listed versions about memorization capacity, architecture comparisons, optimizer or batch effects, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness, or memorized-example removal.
record.gate_note: The paper reports MAML and Sharp-MAML few-shot accuracy, plus train-to-test error comparisons for Sharp-MAMLboth. Its loss-landscape figures are described qualitatively. Cited results from other studies are not extracted.
record.test_reason: The study uses the sharpness–generalization connection to develop Sharp-MAML and evaluates its method's performance. It does not test V7's magnitude-aware perturbation measure or its correlation and ranking of generalization gaps. Its Euclidean perturbation objective, qualitative landscapes, and few-shot performance comparisons do not test any other listed version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the authors' conclusion: applying SAM at either or both MAML stages improves generalization, and applying it only during fine-tuning offers their preferred performance–computation trade-off. The corrected tables agree with the direction of this conclusion. The authors also present convergence and generalization-bound analyses and computationally efficient variants.
record.recipe_differences: Few-shot meta-learning on Mini-Imagenet and Omniglot, using SAM with Adam as base optimizer; evaluates MAML rather than standard single-level training and does not use random labels.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and shot setting change the outcome: Sharp-MAMLlow and Sharp-MAMLup score below reproduced MAML on Mini-Imagenet 5-way 5-shot, while the reported Omniglot variants score above reproduced MAML. Perturbation radii αlow and αup are varied; the text says variants outperform MAML for almost all tested values but does not provide recoverable numeric values in the supplied figure text.

fits_no_version.finding: All three Sharp-MAML variants exceed reproduced MAML accuracy in each reported dataset and shot setting. Correct Mini-Imagenet baselines are 47.13% for 1-shot and 62.20% for 5-shot; 5-shot Sharp-MAMLlow/up accuracies are 63.18%/63.06%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adding SAM to either or both stages of MAML can improve held-out few-shot classification accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: Sharp-MAMLboth has reported generalization errors of 34.58%/8.56%, versus MAML's 37.46%/11.58%, for Mini-Imagenet 1-shot/5-shot.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sharp-MAMLboth reduces reported generalization error relative to MAML in these few-shot settings.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning, Proceedings of the 39th International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 162, 2022
record.problems: Reported best results from three random seeds, but no uncertainty estimates are given. One stated textual summary conflicts with Table 2 for Sharp-MAMLlow in Mini-Imagenet 5-way 5-shot. The α ablation results are figure-only in the supplied text. Comparison against MAML accounts for extra computation by allowing MAML twice as many epochs and selecting its best score across standard or doubled epochs.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. External baseline methods in Tables 1, 2, 4, and 5 are not extracted because they are not the study's Sharp-MAML interventions or the MAML reference.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, natural-label generalization under the same recipe, and chance held-out accuracy with random labels.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed to interpolate.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that recover performance.
Dropout effects, including dependence on training-set size and data augmentation.

Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance correlated with generalization gaps among similarly fitted networks, and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures. Qualitative landscape plots and a SAM intervention do not establish these results.
Removing highly memorized examples versus removing equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The flattened Mini-Imagenet tables caused baseline and value misalignment; Table 3 independently confirms the 47.13% MAML baseline. Remove the record's claimed Mini-Imagenet reversals and textual inconsistency. All row states are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8 because none measures a listed version. Theoretical bounds and qualitative landscapes do not supply a missing V7 test.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence; chance performance on random-label test data.
Width sweep beyond interpolation and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizer comparisons and tuning conditions.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout comparisons across training-set sizes and augmentation conditions.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, its ranking of generalization gaps against other measures, and the stated correlation.
Removing highly memorized examples and comparing with random-example removal.
